aspectTitle: Error identified in text but no correction suggestion given, though the fix is clearly knowable
aspectDescription: This is the central, distinctive obligation of 3.3.3 versus 3.3.1: the page DOES identify the error in text (so 3.3.1 passes and any 'is there an error message' heuristic is satisfied), but the message stops at naming the problem and never tells the user HOW TO FIX it, even though the correction is plainly knowable from the field's constraints. Examples: 'Invalid date' with no format given, 'Password not strong enough' with no rules listed, 'Invalid entry' for a field that accepts exactly one of a small enumerated set. The required human judgment is twofold: (1) is a correction knowable here,
scenario: Travis County homestead-exemption form, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field holds a real but misshapen value (3-7-1965); server accepts only MM/DD/YYYY. The associated error reads only 'Invalid date.' with no format, example, or hint anywhere on the page, though the correction is trivially knowable.
mechanism: Bare restatement of a format error: the message names the error in text (3.3.1 passes) but omits the knowable fixed accepted format (MM/DD/YYYY), so a screen-reader/cognitive user is told THAT it is wrong but never HOW to fix it.

aspectTitle: Suggestion text is present but wrong, misleading, or contradicts the actual validation rule
aspectDescription: The page provides a confident, specific correction suggestion, so every 'a suggestion is present' check passes — but the suggestion is factually incorrect for this field: it names the wrong format, the wrong allowed range, a 'did-you-mean' value that is itself invalid, or a fix the validator will still reject. This is the direct analogue of 'alt exists but misrepresents the image.' Per Trusted Tester the obligation is that the guidance provides SUFFICIENT/ADEQUATE detail to fix the error; a misleading suggestion fails that even though text exists. Only a human who knows the field's true rule c
scenario: Credit-union online-banking password setup. A visible policy box states 'at least 12 characters' and the field enforces minlength=12, but the confident, announced error suggestion says 'Use at least 8 characters to continue.' Following the suggestion (an 8-char password) re-fails.
mechanism: On failed submit a role=alert region (aria-describedby-linked) announces a specific corrective threshold of 8 characters, but the field's enforced minimum is 12; the only corrective guidance offered names a value the field rejects, so acting on it loops the user back to the same error.

aspectTitle: Suggestion correctly WITHHELD for a security/purpose-sensitive field (exception that must read as PASS)
aspectDescription: The SC explicitly carves out 'unless it would jeopardize the security or purpose of the content.' A correct implementation of a security-sensitive field (login password, security-question answer, 2FA code, payment CVV) deliberately gives a generic, non-revealing error and offers no specific correction — and that is the right outcome, a PASS. The hard human judgment is recognizing when withholding a suggestion is correct (and must not be flagged) versus when the same generic message ('Invalid input') on a non-sensitive field is a real failure. This inverts the naive heuristic: here the absence
scenario: Webmail login in the post-submit failed-login state. A single generic 'Email or password is incorrect. Please try again.' governs the credential pair, deliberately not revealing which half was wrong and offering no field-specific correction. The security exception applies (anti-enumeration), so withholding the suggestion is the correct, conformant outcome.
mechanism: A role=alert error referenced by both email and password inputs via aria-describedby announces a generic credential failure plus the only non-jeopardizing correction ('try again'); a field-specific suggestion would leak whether the email exists or that the password was close, which the SC 3.3.3 security/purpose exception forbids, so the absence of a specific suggestion is required, not a defect.

Instead of a generic withheld message, the author gives an over-helpful suggestion that turns the field into a brute-force oracle: 'Almost! Your first 3 digits (4 1 9) are correct, but the code has 6 digits and you entered 5...'. Confirming the correct prefix and exact length collapses the code's entropy. mechanism: #otp-error (role=alert, tied to the six-input one-time-code group via aria-describedby) supplies partial-match feedback that confirms which leading digits matched and the exact expected length; this comparative oracle materially reduces the work to defeat the second factor, jeopardizing the security/purpose of the 2FA code — the disclosure the SC 3.3.3 exception forbids — so a well-formed suggestion still fails.

aspectTitle: Correction not knowable: no suggestion required and absence must not be penalized (the DNA/precondition gate)
aspectDescription: 3.3.3 only obliges a suggestion when 'suggestions for correction are known.' For free-form fields where the correct value is genuinely not inferable by the system (a free-text 'Tell us why', an open-ended display name, a one-time human-verified value), no specific suggestion is possible and the page conformantly provides only a generic 'This field is required' or 'We couldn't verify this.' The judge must decide whether the correction is knowable at all before deciding pass/fail — a precondition gate that distinguishes 'no suggestion because none is possible' (PASS/DNA) from 'no suggestion desp
scenario: E-commerce returns flow in post-submit error state: a required free-text 'Reason for return' textarea was left empty and shows only 'Please tell us your reason for return — this field is required.' No specific suggestion is offered, and none is possible because the field collects open-ended prose. Canonical knowability-gate PASS.
mechanism: The only knowable rule for an open prose 'reason' field is non-empty, which the associated error states. SC 3.3.3 obliges a suggestion only when one is known; for a free-text reason the correct value is not inferable or enumerable, so the generic required-message is the conformant maximum. AT hears a complete, correct, sufficient message via aria-describedby; there is no missing suggestion to provide.

Please choose another.' — no alternatives suggested. aspectTitle: Color/asterisk/icon-only error indication with no text suggestion — the 'in text' limb
aspectDescription: The page communicates that a field is in error and what to do purely through non-text means: turning the label red, adding a red asterisk, swapping in a warning icon, or showing a red border — with NO text description of the problem or the correction. G84 explicitly states this is insufficient: an asterisk or red label does not satisfy the SC; a text description is required. The judgment is visual and semantic: confirm that the red/icon is the ONLY carrier of the error+fix information and that no equivalent text suggestion accompanies it. The 3.3.3-specific limb is the missing CORRECTION TEXT,
scenario: Nonprofit one-time donation form, server-rendered after rejecting a £3 gift (£5 processor minimum). The 'Other amount' field is flagged ONLY by a red label + 2px red border + pink fill via a .is-error class. No error summary, no inline message, no aria-invalid, no hidden text, no title — the knowable correction ('enter £5 or more') is stated nowhere.
mechanism: A detected input error whose correction is knowable (the £5 floor) is conveyed solely by colour (red label + red border + pink background). The input is plain type=text with a well-formed value '3', so validity.valid===true and the accessibility tree exposes invalid:false — a screen reader announces the field identically to a valid one and there is no text suggestion of the accepted value anywhere. G84: an asterisk/red label does not satisfy the SC; text is required.

scenario: PASS twin — higher-ed LMS course-registration confirmation, re-rendered after the term-start date was typed 'Aug 25 2026' when MM/DD/YYYY is required. The field shows the SAME visual treatment as the failing twins (red warning triangle + red border + pink fill) BUT also renders a text correction 'Enter the term start date as MM/DD/YYYY — for example, 08/25/2026.' tied to the input via aria-describedby with aria-invalid=true.
